definitions.explanation: A dog that shows unwavering loyalty to its owner. The word is strongly associated with the famous story of Hachikō, the Akita dog who waited at Shibuya Station for his deceased owner for years.

notes:
Composed of {忠|ちゅう} (loyalty, faithfulness) + {犬|けん} (dog). Almost inseparable from the story of {忠犬|ちゅうけん}ハチ{公|こう} (Hachikō), the Akita dog who continued to wait at Shibuya Station every day for his owner, Professor Ueno, even after the professor died in 1925. A bronze statue of Hachikō at Shibuya Station is one of Tokyo's most famous meeting spots.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {忠犬|ちゅうけん}ハチ{公|こう}: Hachikō, the loyal dog
- {忠犬|ちゅうけん}ハチ{公|こう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{像|ぞう}→像：03691_zou⟧: statue of Hachikō
- {忠犬|ちゅうけん}ハチ{公|こう}⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧: in front of the Hachikō statue (common meeting spot)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The Hachikō story is one of Japan's most beloved tales of animal loyalty and is taught in schools. The phrase {忠犬|ちゅうけん} is sometimes used figuratively to describe a person who is extremely loyal or devoted.
